set.st: An 1874 letter from Gorton L. Scott, left in charge of the Ottawa House after the Port Sheldon land bubble burst, says two strangers who stopped there one October night were murdered by 'Irish Mike' and Dennis, and their bodies and 'some of the plunder' were buried 'near the run at the base of the blow-hole, just west of the hotel'. Scott searched about 1871, but 'shifting sands' had changed the bluffs. By 1899 every vestige of Port Sheldon was gone and strangers were seen surveying and digging there (Grand Haven Tribune); the hotel's shore is still unconfirmed. Pin is a dune blowout at the W edge of a level terrace on the S shore of the outlet (1 m lidar), the best fit for the letter, not a proven spot.
pinev: 1876 Ottawa-Kent atlas, Olive Twp (T6N R16W): Pigeon Lake straddles secs 15/16 and 21/22; the only buildings are a small cluster (one starred) at the outlet, S shore, NW sec 21; the head of the lake (sec 15) has none and no hotel is labelled. The 1874 letter's 'blow-hole just west of the hotel' fits the Lake Michigan dune ridge at the outlet, not the head.
1 m lidar: the channel is at about 42.899; the N side is modified by the power plant. The S side has a shoreline knoll/bench at 42.8986,-86.2108 beside the 1876 building cluster.
1 m lidar: a level terrace (hotel-platform candidate) at 42.8970-42.8983 / -86.2093 to -86.2053.
1 m lidar: the largest dune blowout bowl lies W/SW of the terrace at 42.8967,-86.2098 (a second hollow at 42.8960,-86.2136).

1 m lidar: a straight cut to the shore at about 42.8983,-86.2115, possibly a ditch, i.e. 'the run'. Together these match the 1874 letter: 'near the run at the base of the blow-hole, just west of the hotel'.
Meima's map reading (head of lake) set aside.
set.pl: S shore at the Pigeon Lake outlet: level terrace (hotel platform?) with a dune blowout at its W edge and a straight cut to the shore (1 m lidar), beside the 1876 building cluster

set.st: About 1849 ('about 25 years' before 1874) John McArdill, a jewellery pedlar from London, Canada, was robbed of $4,000-5,000 in coin, watches and jewellery. A deathbed letter from the thief, dated 12 Sep 1873 and postmarked Branch County, said the loot was in a dry well on the south side of the Kalamazoo River in the Newbre neighbourhood, at a stated distance from the old graveyard and about eighty paces from the road, the well filled with oak stumps. The well was found on N. A. Burton's lot as described. On 10 Sep 1874 McArdill's diggers hit the stumps about 40 ft down, and on 24 Sep the Detroit News reported that he 'has got to the bottom of his well at last, and has found no treasure … a disappointed and disgusted man.' The Free Press of the same day says six men had widened the well to 10 ft and the work was given up on 22 Sep 1874 after about $200 was spent; its theories were that the other robber had already taken the money, that the letter was cooked up on a medium's advice, or that it was a grudge hoax. By late October 'the belief has become almost universal' that McArdill got the money on the last day: a neighbour said the diggers had not reached bottom when he went to dinner and were hastily filling the hole when he came back. Pin is the best well candidate on 1 m lidar near the half-mile stake the letter paced from, not a confirmed fix. The Free Press of 15 Sep 1874 adds that the well had been filled 12-14 years earlier and cropped over, and that the diggers were McArdill and his son, the well-digger Joe Jackson and three labourers.
pinev: 1873 plat: N. A. Burton 160 = NW¼ sec 27 T2S R7W; Newbre farms across the S-line road; letter's paces put the well within ~120 m of the W quarter corner beside the 27/28 road.
W quarter corner from BLM PLSS (42.26852,-85.12030); the 27/28 road still shows on 2017 Michigan 1 m lidar; dry farmland.

The 1873 plat shows the graveyard at the SW corner of sec 27, matching the letter's graveyard reference; the well lies between it and the W quarter corner along the 27/28 road, nearer the quarter corner by the paces.

Free Press 15 Sep 1874: the well was about 5 mi SE of Battle Creek and about a mile from the Kalamazoo River, in N. A. Burton's pasture lot; the reporter paced from 'the half-mile stake' and found the distances exactly as the letter gave, which fits the W quarter corner of sec 27.

1894 Calhoun plat: no Burton or McArdill by then; at the W quarter of sec 27, E. Sanford 80, J. G. Ulrich 78 and H. C. Webster 39 N of the CJ&M railroad and an unlabelled 79 S of it; Newbre still in secs 34-35.

Lidar at the W quarter corner of sec 27 (42.2685,-85.1203; road and quarter line confirmed), E side: A, a round depression at 42.2676,-85.1197 (about 100 m S, 50 m E of the corner), the best dry-well candidate.
B: a small rimmed pit at 42.2694,-85.1195.
C: two small knobs about 150 m E of the corner.
A sits farther from the N-S road (about 50 m) than the letter's 8 paces, so it is a candidate, not a fix.

1894 plat: C. O. Tower in NE¼ sec 29 T9N R9W where a road meets the NW shore; state lidar shows a ~300 m cut bank between the old road and the shore, centred about 43.140,-85.395; r200 covers the bank
Kent County parks layer (ArcGIS): the pin is inside Wabasis County Park, about 70 m from its north edge; the r200 ring runs slightly past the boundary onto private land.
1 m lidar: sharpest cut bank 43.1406,-85.3946 (confirms the pin), ravine pair 43.1388,-85.3970, S-shore scarps 43.137,-85.3914; all inside the county park, look only.
Placed from the source text: PLACEHOLDER on Crow Creek (GNIS), Whitefield Twp T13N R9E; claim "partly prairie, partly timbered bluff"
Unconfirmed, one source

Records of the Olden Time (Marshall Co, 1880): the Reeves homestead stood in the mouth of a deep ravine on Reeves' Run, about equidistant from Sparland and Henry, N of Talliaferro's (later the James Winship place), Whitefield Twp; no section given.
